scope: Common (themes/common) and future themes explicitly created for this collection. These are the collection author's design rules, not Widgetizer platform requirements or defaults for other authors.

rules.instruction: Follow the Widgetizer design skill's brief and question process, then build one standalone responsive static homepage and separate styleguide for owner approval before Widgetizer conversion. Carry existing answers forward and ask only about material unresolved choices. Base the direction on that skill, the supplied brief and these collection rules, rather than unrelated design workflows or external style catalogs.
rules.implementation: Keep static prototypes separate from installable themes. Open the pages in the browser for the owner; never hand over links. Refine the actual pages until explicitly approved; do not create Widgetizer theme files before that approval. Preserve the approved prototype and reuse its markup/styles/assets during conversion. Once the theme is built, review the theme itself; do not compare it point by point with the prototype. Individual image assets may be generated when useful; generated website mockups are not the review artifact.

rules.instruction: Use uppercase subtitles, eyebrows and small labels only in languages whose casing has been checked. Keep Greek in natural case with its accents; do not apply automatic uppercase or strip accents from stored text. Preserve natural case for unverified languages.
rules.implementation: Store natural-case text. Scope any CSS uppercase treatment to verified languages using the element's inherited language; account for regional language codes and nested language overrides.

rules.instruction: Never decorate subtitles or eyebrows with bullets, dots, numbers, dashes, em dashes or ornamental separators. Use plain text. This applies to authored content, CSS pseudo-elements and generated counters.
examplesToRemove: A leading dot before a subtitle

rules.instruction: When a button or action link has an icon, use an actual SVG from a suitable open-source icon set. Do not substitute Unicode characters, text glyphs or CSS-drawn approximations. Keep the icons visually consistent and retain their source and license. Tabler is an example, not a required dependency. Icons are optional, not mandatory for every button.

Button corners follow the site settings, as in Arch: Shapes sets the corners of buttons, cards, images and form fields, and Button shape can override them for buttons. Each theme only chooses their defaults. Apply the result consistently to primary, secondary and icon-only buttons, including navigation and disclosure controls.
rules.implementation: Use the radius tokens the settings drive for every button and control and in every interaction state; never a fixed radius. Review the full page and styleguide together, including small controls, rather than checking only the main calls to action.

rules.instruction: Choose text-only or icon-assisted buttons and action links deliberately. Actively consider icons where they clarify the action or destination; restraint should not lead to avoiding useful iconography altogether. Do not automatically append the same arrows to actions across themes, or rotate through unrelated icons merely for variety. Arrows remain appropriate when their directional meaning helps. Keep related actions consistent within a theme, and review the collection for repeated habits in icon use.
rules.example: Margin's book enquiries and reading-club invitation work as text-only actions. The mobile menu controls and back-to-top arrow retain their clear functional purpose.

rules.instruction: Never use numbers merely to decorate sections, cards, captions or other theme elements. Remove decorative number controls as well as their output and demo values. Numbers that communicate real information, such as prices, quantities or meaningful ordered steps, remain appropriate.

Default to one consistent color and typographic treatment within a heading. Do not routinely highlight selected words or a second line with another color, italics, font or weight as a decorative flourish. Mixed treatments are allowed only when they make a specific, meaningful contribution to the content or design; be able to explain that contribution. Visual variety alone is not a sufficient reason.
rules.example: Kiln's 'Made slowly. Lived with.' expresses one thought. Both lines use the same upright type and color; the line break provides enough structure.

rules.instruction: A page or section introduction reads top to bottom in one column: eyebrow, heading, then the description. Never split the heading and its description into side-by-side columns; the eye has to jump across the page to read one thought.
rules.implementation: Stack the three, start-aligned, with the description at a readable measure under the heading. The split introduction on Goodmove’s services page was refused: it broke the reading flow and looked empty.

rules.instruction: Use a minimum of 16px for body text, navigation, buttons and form text. Reserve 14px for short secondary labels, captions and metadata; no visible theme text should fall below 14px. These are minimums, not target sizes: increase them when the chosen typeface needs more room to read comfortably. Keep these floors on mobile; adapt spacing and layout instead of shrinking text to fit.
rules.implementation: Express the sizes in relative units that respect the visitor's font preferences: at a default 16px root, use at least 1rem for primary text and 0.875rem for secondary text. Do not reduce the root font size to evade the minimums. Check computed sizes and visual readability in desktop and mobile previews, including fluid type and responsive overrides. This collection preference addresses type size only; the later accessibility review must also assess contrast, zoom, spacing and interaction.

rules.instruction: Judge typography by the shape and rhythm of the rendered text as well as font choice and size. Avoid awkward isolated words, markedly uneven heading lines and cramped wrapping on desktop and mobile. Coordinate text width, type size and layout proportions; do not rely on hard-coded English line breaks or nonbreaking phrases to make a reusable theme work.
rules.review: Inspect actual line breaks at desktop, intermediate and phone widths, including longer edited copy and representative translations. CSS text balancing and a no-overflow result are aids, not evidence that the text looks good.
rules.example: Alder's initial hero isolated 'worth' between 'Somewhere' and 'slowing down.' despite fitting within the viewport. That composition needed correction.

rules.instruction: Use a deliberate, shared grid for the page's section layouts. Establish consistent content boundaries, column tracks and gutters; build section compositions on that structure rather than positioning each group independently. Different sections may span different numbers of columns, but their alignment must follow the shared grid. Build balanced layouts around clear content relationships and a logical reading order. Complexity, staggered placement and asymmetry must serve the content. Do not scatter items around a photograph or create arbitrary empty areas merely to make a layout different. Using CSS Grid alone does not establish a coherent composition.
rules.implementation: Define shared content-width and gutter tokens and use CSS Grid for the section columns. Choose the column count to suit the theme; twelve columns are not mandatory. Check the actual rendered edges of the header, hero and supporting sections, and align section introductions with the related columns beneath them. Do not treat a no-overflow result as evidence that alignment is correct. Keep an explanation, its action and supporting note visibly grouped. Let columns and rows grow with content; review longer headings, paragraphs and translated button labels at desktop, intermediate and phone widths. Assess whitespace and alignment across the whole section, including its right edge and adjacent sections. Check whether labels, headings, imagery and body copy form an immediately understandable group; matching column edges alone is not enough. Preserve meaningful layout variety without adding complexity for its own sake. Use one explicit shared column system, such as twelve or twenty-four columns, with consistent tracks and gutters across page sections. Header, hero, supporting content and footer must share deliberate outer boundaries; do not introduce unrelated maximum widths for individual sections. Verify alignment at wide desktop widths as well as tablet and phone sizes, including the author’s supplied screenshot dimensions when available.
rules.example: Accord's initial engagement section aligned its columns but left two small labels isolated above a photograph while the main heading occupied the opposite column. The empty area and detached introduction made the composition unclear. Recompose the section around one clear introduction and a balanced relationship between the image and story; do not preserve the arrangement merely because it uses a grid.

rules.instruction: Compose each section across the full content width. A heading, paragraph and actions pressed into one half of a band with the other half empty is not a composition. Centre balanced content, such as a call to action with one message and one main action, or place the parts across the columns with a reason for each placement.
rules.implementation: Check every band at desktop width for an unused half; the call-to-action band is the usual offender. Goodmove’s services page had its call to action pressed into the left half and was refused.

rules.instruction: Use a restrained, consistent set of real open-source icons more often where they help visitors scan practical information: location, opening hours, contact methods, service details or ingredient labels. Keep meaningful text beside them, and make sure the symbol matches the content. Do not attach icons to every heading or use them as ornamental eyebrow markers. Match stroke weight, size and alignment across the theme.

Premium themes must show a clear increase in design care and detail, even for a small business. Develop the whole page beyond a pleasing palette, fonts and hero: compose each section deliberately, give photographs and useful information appropriate emphasis, refine spacing and alignment, and finish interaction states. Make layouts express the theme's intended character while keeping content relationships clear.

Use new explorations to test meaningfully different page compositions and widget layouts as well as colors and typography. Directions may range from restrained to forceful. Avoid repeating the same large headline, photograph and alternating split sections across the collection. Choose layouts that help the niche's content, interaction and visitor goals, express the theme's intended character and remain easy to edit.

Every new theme exploration must make a deliberate attempt at a distinct hero composition. This is a requirement, not an optional refinement. Compare the proposed opening with the collection's existing heroes before building it; changing only colors, fonts, copy or imagery does not establish a new composition. Aim for as much meaningful uniqueness as the niche and content allow.
rules.implementation: Record the closest existing hero and explain the new opening's different content hierarchy, image/text relationship or useful interaction in the working brief. Build around the niche's visitor needs. Novelty must still make visual sense: clear grouping, balanced grid proportions, legible type, considered crops and a logical mobile reading order. Do not introduce arbitrary shapes, staggered elements or complexity simply to look different.
rules.review: Review the hero beside relevant earlier explorations, then inspect desktop, intermediate, phone and longer/translated text. If the composition still repeats an earlier hero without a content-led reason, revise it before presenting the theme. Retain accepted palettes and typography when feedback concerns composition only.
rules.example: Mova opens with a photographic dance-studio invitation beside a practical first-class panel, instead of the collection's familiar large heading above a wide photograph.

rules.instruction: Use lines and borders when they clarify a specific relationship or contribute intentional character. Prefer spacing, alignment and grouping when these already separate the content clearly. Avoid stacking the last item border, a section border and a pricing border around the same transition. Review adjacent sections together, not only each widget in isolation.
rules.example: Rows of image-with-text sections and side-by-side quotes need no rule between or above them; their spacing already separates them. Rules there were refused on Goodmove’s services page.

rules.instruction: The last section before the footer never shares the footer’s colour scheme. Two dark bands on top of each other read as one block: the call to action loses its edge and the footer stops reading as the end of the page.
rules.implementation: Give the closing call to action its own scheme, usually the theme’s accent band, and let the footer be the only block in its colour. Decided on Goodmove’s services page: the call to action moved from the dark scheme to the yellow one.

rules.instruction: Give practical visitor information such as location, opening hours and pricing a clear hierarchy with meaningful headings and tightly grouped related values. Keep day/time and label/value pairs close enough to read together. Tie actions to the information they serve. Design normal, hover and keyboard-focus states as one coherent treatment; avoid accidental doubled underlines, layout jumps or lost contrast.

Choose motion that suits the theme's intended character and visitor needs. Gentle reveals, crisp transitions or no animation can all be appropriate. Use considered timing; avoid making visitors wait for content or animating every element independently.
rules.implementation: Respect reduced-motion preferences, keep content available when animation or JavaScript is disabled, and support widgets added or re-rendered in the editor. Arch's assets/reveal.js and related styles are an implementation reference; adapt the treatment to each theme.

rules.instruction: Complete premium themes are built on the shared premium source, which follows Arch: shared tokens for recurring design decisions in base.css, a common foundation for reusable elements, and scoped CSS per widget for its specific layout and appearance. A theme sets its look through its settings defaults; its own widgets carry their own scoped CSS. No theme restyles a shared widget.
rules.implementation: Keep widget-specific styles with their widget and load them through the app's supported asset mechanism, as illustrated by themes/arch/widgets/video-popup/. Avoid accumulating widget styling in one global stylesheet.

rules.instruction: Ship a selected footer legal menu with working destinations and clearly labelled replace-before-publishing sample legal pages. Demo sites should show several social networks using network homepage URLs in Project details. Use consistent action appearance for comparable adjacent sections; use secondary buttons for image-with-text detail actions unless there is a purposeful hierarchy. Keep desktop navigation compact without reducing readable type or mobile touch targets. Verify palette borders against both main and secondary backgrounds.
rules.implementation: Check these defaults in the starter source and a newly created or isolated demonstration project, not only a manually edited preview. Social profiles belong to Project details; do not hardcode them in shared widgets.

rules.instruction: Use an existing widget when its purpose and content blocks fit. Add a reusable layout when positioning differs. One theme can establish the need. Create a separate widget only for different content, behaviour or requirements that cannot share a clear editing model. Use generic widget and layout names.
rules.implementation: Keep standard block controls and their behaviour consistent. Starter content chooses sizes, text treatment and button styles through settings. CSS must not override those choices. Preserve existing layout defaults. Verify heading and text sizes, muted text, both button styles and sizes, spacing and colours. Save, reload and check the result. Test affected earlier-theme examples when shared source changes.
rules.example: Common uses Call to action with the Split layout. It is not a separate Split invitation widget. Opening hours stay in the footer.

heroVariations: Develop transparent headers over hero imagery and text-on-image heroes as useful options for the collection, starting with the Panna preview. Treat them as independent choices: text on an image can also sit beneath a solid header. Overlay navigation only when the opening widget supports it; other pages need a readable solid header. Compose and review the image, text contrast, navigation contrast and mobile crop together. Carry these options into full theme development where suitable.

presetStrategy.intent: Each retained theme will have 1–3 distinct presets showing its range. Presets may span related businesses with compatible content and editing needs, or very different locations and moods within one business type. They are not restricted to one exact niche.
presetStrategy.design: Give each preset a coherent combination of imagery, palette, typography, content and available layout choices. Vary section selection, order and emphasis where useful. Plan enough flexibility in the shared theme widgets and settings to support these differences while keeping owner editing simple.

examples.sharedNeeds: Personal introduction, lesson options, teaching approach and enquiries
Rooms, the property, local experiences, practical stay information and enquiries

presetStrategy.scope: Explore unique industries and niches first, checking the existing collection for overlap before recommending another exploration. Review the collection before developing each theme’s 1–3 presets; these examples guide flexibility and do not require building variants during initial exploration.

boundary: These rules do not prohibit ordinary punctuation in sentences or markers in genuine content lists.
review: Review the entire page and its source: expression of the intended character, composition and level of finish, practical information hierarchy, adjacent separators, purposeful content and action icons, consistent button shape, hover and focus states, CSS-generated decoration, captions, language-specific casing, meaningful heading treatments, and type sizes and readability at desktop and mobile widths. Review motion timing and reduced-motion behavior when motion is introduced; check token use and widget CSS organization during full theme development. Structural theme validation alone does not check these collection rules.
